independence: Written from the source of each repository at its pinned commit, read with git and grep, before any evaluation run exists. Kalyth's analyzer, impact traversal, context compiler and agents were not run on either scenario while writing it, and no context package for either scenario was read. For scenario template-tenancy-complete the writer read the recorded Navigator alternatives (deploy/demo/recordings/recordings.json, alternative A1), because the protocol takes that scenario's decision from them, and the demo walkthrough's account of earlier agent runs. Any later change is a new version with a new SHA-256, published with its evidence and applied to every arm; nothing is ever changed toward Kalyth's output.
unit: Files are repository-relative paths of files that exist at the pinned commit. 'required' files are changed by every correct, complete implementation; 'acceptable' files may or may not change depending on design and are not penalised; any other changed existing file is out of scope. Where a scenario's files block has role 'diagnostic', its 'required' and 'acceptable' sets describe the expected per-route implementation and are not requirements: correctness rests on the acceptance checks and on element and endpoint completeness, and an implementation that changes fewer or different files is not penalised for it. New files are listed for context and not scored at file level. Elements are scored from the diff by the blind reviewer, by behaviour wherever the change sits; acceptance checks are run by the scorer.

scenarios.request: Make every AutoGen Studio API endpoint act as the authenticated user. Today most routes take a user_id query parameter or body field and trust it, so any client can read or change another user's teams, sessions, runs, messages, galleries and settings. Change the backend so that the user is always the one the existing authentication established (request.state.user, set by AuthMiddleware; with auth type "none" this is the default user), and a user_id sent by a client is ignored. Every read, list, create, update and delete of Team, Session, Run, Message, Gallery and Settings rows must be limited to rows owned by that user; a row owned by another user is reported as not found (404) and is never changed. Rows created through the API get the authenticated user's id. The run WebSocket (/api/ws/runs/{run_id}) must check ownership before it registers the connection, and must close a connection that does not own the run without affecting the owner's run; its existing exception for the admin role stays, and is the only role exception (see the notes). Keep paths, methods and response shapes as they are, so the existing frontend keeps working; do not change the frontend. Add or update backend tests for the new behaviour.
notes: Ignore a client-supplied user_id (query parameter or body field); do not reject the request. The frontend keeps sending it.
Report another user's row as not found (404), not as forbidden.

Keep the run WebSocket's existing exception for the admin role, and keep it as narrow as it is today: a connection whose token carries the role "admin" may open /api/ws/runs/{run_id} for a run it does not own. Check it together with ownership, before the connection is registered. It is the only role exception, and it applies to that WebSocket only: no HTTP endpoint gives the admin role, or any other role, access to another user's rows.
Out of scope: the MCP endpoints (/api/mcp/...), the validation endpoints, the auth endpoints, authentication itself (providers, tokens, middleware), the database schema and the frontend.
acceptanceCriteria: Every Team, Session, Run, Message, Gallery and Settings endpoint acts as the authenticated user; a user_id query parameter or body field sent by the client has no effect.
Listing returns only the caller's rows; reading, updating or deleting another user's row returns 404 and leaves the row unchanged, whatever roles the caller has.
Rows created through the API are owned by the caller, and a create or update request cannot overwrite another user's row by sending its id.

The run WebSocket closes a connection from a user who neither owns the run nor has the admin role before registering it, and the owner's connection and run continue; a connection with the admin role is accepted for any run, as today.
Paths, methods and response shapes are unchanged, and the frontend is not changed.
Backend tests cover cross-user access for each resource and pass, and the existing tests still pass.

acceptanceChecks.setup: The real app (autogenstudio.web.app) with a temporary SQLite database and app directory, and an auth config of type github with a test jwt_secret, so AuthMiddleware sets request.state.user from a bearer token. Users alice and bob get tokens from AuthManager.create_token with the default roles ["user"]; carol, who owns no rows, gets one with roles ["admin"]. Alice owns team TA, session SA (team TA), run RA (session SA, status active), message MA (run RA, stored with user_id None), gallery GA and settings STA; bob owns TB, SB, RB, GB and STB. Each check sends bob's token unless it says otherwise, and adds ?user_id=alice or a body user_id of alice wherever the route accepts one.

checks.check: GET /api/teams/, /api/sessions/ and /api/gallery/ return none of alice's rows; GET /api/settings/ returns bob's settings, never STA.
GET /api/teams/{TA}, /api/sessions/{SA}, /api/sessions/{SA}/runs and /api/gallery/{GA} return 404.
DELETE /api/teams/{TA}, /api/sessions/{SA} and /api/gallery/{GA} leave the rows in the database.
POST /api/teams/, /api/sessions/ and /api/gallery/ with body user_id alice create rows whose user_id is bob.
POST /api/teams/ with body id TA, POST /api/sessions/ with body id SA and POST /api/gallery/ with body id GA leave alice's rows unchanged.
PUT /api/sessions/{SA} returns 404 and SA is unchanged; PUT /api/sessions/{SB} with body id SA leaves SA unchanged.
PUT /api/gallery/{GA} returns 404 and GA is unchanged; PUT /api/settings/ with body id STA and user_id alice leaves STA unchanged.
POST /api/runs/ with session_id SA and user_id alice returns 404 and creates no run.
GET /api/runs/{RA} and GET /api/runs/{RA}/messages return 404 for bob; as alice, GET /api/runs/{RA}/messages returns MA.

With alice connected to /api/ws/runs/{RA}, bob connects with his token: bob's socket is closed without a 'connected' system message, alice's socket stays registered, and RA is not stopped (its status is unchanged).
Alice connecting to /api/ws/runs/{RA} with her token is accepted and receives the 'connected' system message.
As alice, every endpoint above works on her own rows with the response shape of the base commit ({status, data} or the Response model).
With auth type none, requests without a token act as guestuser@gmail.com: GET /api/teams/ creates and returns a default team owned by that user.
The arm's own tests and the base commit's tests that pass at the base commit pass in the arm's tree; ruff check passes on the changed files.

With no other socket connected to RA, carol connects to /api/ws/runs/{RA} with her admin token: the connection is accepted and receives the 'connected' system message. The owner is not connected at the same time, because the manager keeps one connection per run and the request does not change that.

With carol's admin token: GET /api/teams/, /api/sessions/ and /api/gallery/ with ?user_id=alice return none of alice's rows; GET /api/teams/{TA}, /api/sessions/{SA}, /api/runs/{RA}, /api/runs/{RA}/messages and /api/gallery/{GA} return 404; DELETE /api/sessions/{SA} and PUT /api/gallery/{GA} leave the rows unchanged; GET /api/settings/?user_id=alice never returns STA.

scenarios.role: holdout repository; Kalyth's analyzer was developed on it and the demo uses it, so results here are in-sample
scenarios.commitNote: tag 0.12.0, the commit of the demo template and of the recorded Navigator run
scenarios.request: Add multi-tenancy: every user and item belongs to an organisation. Add an Organisation table (id, name, created_at) and an org_id foreign key to it on User and Item. Regular users work inside their organisation: they list, read, update and delete all items of their organisation, including items other members own, and items of other organisations are reported as not found (404). Superusers keep their current global access. Every new item gets the organisation of the user who creates it. A user created by a superuser through POST /api/v1/users/ joins the organisation named by an optional org_id in the request, or the superuser's own organisation when it is omitted; an org_id that names no organisation is refused with 404. POST /api/v1/users/signup creates a new organisation for the new user, named after their email. POST /api/v1/private/users/ and the first superuser created by init_db use the default organisation, created if missing. No endpoint can change the organisation of an existing user or item. UserPublic and ItemPublic include org_id. Write an Alembic migration after fe56fa70289e that creates the organisation table, adds nullable org_id columns, puts every existing user and item into one organisation named "Default", then makes both columns NOT NULL; its downgrade reverses this. Do not change the frontend or regenerate its client. Update or add backend tests for the new behaviour.
notes: This implements alternative A1, 'Explicit org on both User and Item', of the decision 'Introduce multi-tenancy with organisations'. Philip accepted it with these answers to its open questions: superusers stay global (the current semantics); PostgreSQL in production and in tests; existing data goes into a single default organisation.
Use the column and field name org_id; the organisation table's name is free.
Emails stay globally unique; login, password recovery and password reset are unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: After the migration, user.org_id and item.org_id are NOT NULL foreign keys to the organisation table, every pre-existing row is in one organisation named Default, and the downgrade reverses it.
Regular users list, read, update and delete exactly the items of their own organisation, including items other members own; items of other organisations return 404 and stay unchanged.
Superusers keep global access to users and items.

New items get their creator's organisation. POST /users/ uses the given org_id or the superuser's organisation and refuses an unknown org_id with 404; signup creates a new organisation; the private endpoint and init_db use the default organisation.
No endpoint changes an existing user's or item's organisation, and UserPublic and ItemPublic include org_id.
The frontend and its generated client are unchanged; backend tests are updated or added and pass on PostgreSQL.

decision.source: the recorded Navigator run on the demo template (deploy/demo/recordings, preset multi-tenancy, NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, recorded 2026-10-23), replayed at no cost; alternative A1 accepted by a person with the answers in the notes
decision.recordedRequest: Add multi-tenancy: every user and item belongs to an organisation.
decision.acceptedAlternative: A1, Explicit org on both User and Item: Organisation table; nullable org_id foreign keys on User and Item; all API queries filter by current_user.org_id; superusers bypass the filter; the migration backfills, then sets NOT NULL.

requiredWhy.backend/app/crud.py: create_item builds an Item without org_id, which the NOT NULL column refuses; create_user must place the user in an organisation unless UserCreate carries it, and create_item has no such escape.
requiredWhy.backend/app/api/routes/private.py: builds a User directly, so it must set org_id.
requiredWhy.backend/tests/api/routes/test_items.py: test_read_item_not_enough_permissions, test_update_item_not_enough_permissions and test_delete_item_not_enough_permissions expect 403 for another user's item; under the new rules that item is either shared (200) or in another organisation (404).

acceptanceChecks.setup: PostgreSQL 17 in a container, the arm's tree at its final commit, FASTAPI_ENV=development, migrations applied with alembic upgrade head, init_db run as by the prestart script. Fixtures are created through the API only, so the checks do not depend on table or class names: S is the first superuser (organisation D); UA is created by S through POST /users/ without org_id; UB signs up; UC is created by S with org_id set to UB's organisation; items IA by UA, IS by S, IB by UB.

checks.check: On a database at fe56fa70289e holding 2 users and 3 items, alembic upgrade head leaves user.org_id and item.org_id NOT NULL with foreign keys to one table, and every row in a single organisation named Default; alembic downgrade fe56fa70289e then succeeds and removes the columns and the table.
GET /users/me includes org_id for S, UA, UB and UC; UA has S's organisation, UB's differs from it, UC has UB's.
POST /users/ by S with an org_id that names no organisation returns 404 and creates no user.
An item created by UA has UA's org_id.
GET /items/ as UA lists IA and IS and not IB, with a matching count.
As UA, GET and PUT /items/{IS} return 200, and DELETE of another item S created returns 200.
As UA, GET, PUT and DELETE /items/{IB} return 404 and IB is unchanged.
As S, GET /items/ lists IA, IS and IB, and GET /items/{IB} returns 200.
PUT /items/{IA} by UA, PATCH /users/me by UA and PATCH /users/{UA} by S, each with another org_id in the body, leave the organisation unchanged (ignored or refused with 422).
POST /private/users/ creates a user in S's organisation (the default).
On an empty database after migrations, init_db creates the first superuser in an organisation, and running it twice creates no second organisation.
The arm's backend test suite passes on PostgreSQL, the base commit's tests not touched by the arm still pass, and the template's lint script (ruff and mypy) passes.

staticallyUnknowable.item: How existing users and items of a real deployment should map to organisations; the decision puts them all in Default, which may be wrong for a deployment with several customers.

Whether FASTAPI_ENV enables the private router in a given deployment (runtime configuration).
Query performance with the organisation filter (whether org_id needs an index) depends on data volume and query plans.
How the frontend behaves after the change (the items page now shows other members' items, the admin page shows org_id); it is out of scope and only running it shows this.
